{{Short description|New Zealand-American mathematician}}
'''David Winston Howard Shale''' (22 March 1932, [[New Zealand]] – 7 January 2016) was a New Zealand-American mathematician, specializing in the mathematical foundations of quantum physics.<ref name=Penn>{{cite web|title=In Memoriam, David W. H. Shale 1932–2016|website=Department of Mathematics, University of Pennsylvania|url=https://www.math.upenn.edu/about/department-history/in-memoriam}}</ref> He is known as one of the namesakes of the [[Symplectic spinor bundle|Segal–Shale-Weil representation]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.2307/2034661|jstor=2034661|title=Some Remarks on Symplectic Automorphisms|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|volume=16|issue=3|pages=393–397|year=1965|last1=MacKey|first1=George W.|doi-access=free}}</ref>

After secondary and undergraduate education in New Zealand, Shale became a graduate student in mathematics at the [[University of Chicago]] and received his Ph.D. there in 1960.<ref name=Penn/> His thesis ''On certain groups of operators on Hilbert space'' was written under the supervision of [[Irving Segal]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6495|title=David Winston Howard Shale}}</ref> Shale became an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and then became in 1964 a professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], where he continued teaching until his retirement.<ref name=Penn/>

{{blockquote|He was an expert in the mathematical foundations of Quantum Physics with many very original ideas on the subject. In addition, he discovered what is now called the Shale-Weil Representation in operator theory. He was also an expert in Bayesian Probability Theory, especially as it applied to Physics.<ref name=Penn/>}}

According to Irving Segal:
{{blockquote|... although contrary to common intuitive belief, Lorentz-invariance in itself is materially insufficient to characterize the vacuum for any [[free field]] (this remarkable fact is due to David Shale; it should perhaps be emphasized that this lack of uniqueness holds even in such a simple case as the conventional scalar meson field ...), none of the Lorentz-invariant states other than the conventional vacuum is consistent with the postulate of the positivity of the energy, when suitably and simply formulated.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1215/ijm/1255632508|title=Mathematical characterization of the physical vacuum for a linear Bose-Einstein field|journal=Illinois Journal of Mathematics|volume=6|issue=3|pages=500–523|year=1962|last1=Segal|first1=I. E.|doi-access=free}} (quote from p. 501)</ref>}}
